notes.text: Available in cPanel 136 and later. Deletes the named log archive from the authenticated account's ~/logs directory. The source requires that the filename reside in that directory, end in .gz and contain no path traversal characters. The client forwards the file string unchanged and performs no local filesystem access. Deletion can remove archived logs permanently.

This mutation uses form POST. The pinned data schema is unconstrained: preserve any present JSON value, including null, false, zero, empty strings and opaque objects. An absent data member remains a mismatch. The client performs one request with no retry or rollback. API success does not prove eventual rotation, deletion or retention enforcement.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 82 and later. Retrieves the selected account's archival settings. archive_logs, prune_archive and using_default have public integer 0/1 flag results. retention_days is a number of days; zero retains logs indefinitely. When no custom retention value is set, the returned retention_days is the server-wide default. using_default distinguishes the server default from a custom value. Optional fields remain omitted.

The 2026-10-31 capture on cPanel 11.138.0.19 observed numeric-string wire values for archive_logs, prune_archive and retention_days through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge. Only archive_logs/prune_archive accept exact quoted 0/1 flags, and only retention_days accepts lossless canonical in-range integer strings. Results normalize to the documented integer types. The structural capture does not establish which quoted flag values occurred or prove both values were observed. using_default and sibling operation fields retain their prior strict contracts.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 138 and later. Requires the exact domain selector for a domain owned by the selected account. Returns PHP error log file metadata only, without file contents. file_id identifies php_fpm_error_log (home logs directory), docroot_error_log (website document root) or homedir_error_log (home directory).

modified_today is a strict integer 0/1 flag using server local time. mtime is a Unix timestamp and size is bytes; each may explicitly be null. error is an optional nullable string explaining an unavailable file. Other optional fields retain omission. The client forwards domain unchanged and does not open returned paths.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 82 and later. Saves the selected account's log archival settings using form POST. The source requires at least one of archive_logs, prune_archive or retention_days; each parameter remains optional at the native boundary, with server-side cross-field validation.

archive_logs controls archiving to the home directory after statistics processing. If omitted, its default is archive-logs in ~/.cpanel-logs, or default_archive-logs in cpanel.config when that file is absent. prune_archive controls removing the previous month's archives from ~/logs at month end. Its omitted default is remove-old-archived-logs in ~/.cpanel-logs, or default_remove-old-archive-logs in cpanel.config when the file is absent. Explicit false flags are sent as zero.

retention_days is in days: zero retains logs indefinitely; -1 clears the per-user override and restores the server default; positive integers retain logs for that many days. Omission preserves the existing value. Pruning and retention can remove archives. No client-side minimum or enum validation is added.

The pinned data schema is unconstrained: preserve any present JSON value, including null, false, zero, empty strings and opaque objects. An absent data member remains a mismatch. The client performs one request with no retry or rollback. API success does not prove eventual rotation, deletion or retention enforcement.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 138 and later. Requires domain owned by the selected account and the exact file_id selector: php_fpm_error_log (home logs directory), docroot_error_log (domain document root), or homedir_error_log (home directory). Selectors are strings sent unchanged; the client does not access the local filesystem.

Reads trailing PHP error log lines in chronological order, oldest first. Omitted limit retains the server default of 100; the documented minimum is 1 and values above 5000 are silently capped by the server. The client sends the supplied integer unchanged.

log_content is a potentially sensitive string list and is empty for an empty log. Do not log response content or PayloadMismatchException payloads. lines_read is the returned line count; partial=1 means the file exceeds limit. modified_today uses the server date/time. mtime and size come from fstat and remain integer Unix time and bytes. Flags remain strict integer 0/1; optional fields retain omission. Returning API success does not establish HTTP enforcement or log rotation.
